reasoning: This is FairTix's automated customer support triage system. When new support messages arrive in a Google Sheet, the workflow: 1) Uses Claude AI to classify messages into categories (FAQ, Payment/Billing, Account/Verification, etc.) and sentiment (positive/neutral/frustrated/angry), 2) Routes FAQ questions to automated responses using their FAQ document content, 3) Escalates complex issues (Payment/Billing) to human support via email notification, 4) Updates the sheet with classifications and auto-generated responses. The extensive AI prompt reveals FairTix is a fair ticket marketplace with features like fair queues, resale caps, and verification. The 12% error rate with 362 versions suggests active development/refinement. The workflow replaces manual ticket sorting and basic FAQ responses.
name: Customer Support Triage & Auto-Response System
businessNarrative: FairTix operates an AI-powered customer support system that automatically classifies incoming tickets and provides instant responses to common questions. The system distinguishes between simple FAQ queries (queue mechanics, pricing) and complex issues requiring human intervention (payment disputes, account problems). This reveals FairTix as a sophisticated ticket marketplace with fair queue systems, price transparency, and resale controls - positioning them as an ethical alternative to traditional ticketing. The automated FAQ responses maintain customer satisfaction while freeing support staff for complex issues.
trigger: New customer support message added to Google Sheet
dataFlow: Support messages enter via Google Sheet → AI classifies category/sentiment → FAQ messages get auto-responses from FAQ document → Complex issues escalate to human support via email → All classifications and responses stored back in sheet

impact.reasoning: High impact - this is the primary customer support interface. Failures mean customers get no response to inquiries, potentially losing sales and damaging brand trust. The 12% error rate is concerning for a customer-facing system.
impact.failureScenario: Customers receive no acknowledgment of support requests, leading to frustration and potential churn. FAQ responses fail to generate, requiring manual intervention for basic questions. Support team misses escalated tickets, creating service delays. Misclassification could route urgent payment issues to FAQ responses or overwhelm human agents with simple questions.
impact.revenueConnection: Direct - unresolved support issues can block ticket purchases, prevent problem resolution, and damage customer relationships leading to lost sales and negative reviews

detectability.reasoning: Partially monitored - executions are tracked (50 total, 12% error rate visible) but no explicit error handling or alerting configured. Support team would notice missing email notifications for escalated cases.
detectability.evidence: Execution statistics available but no retry logic, error workflows, or explicit monitoring nodes. Support team email notifications provide some failure detection for escalated cases.

If 20% of delays result in lost sales = 1.2 lost sales/day at avg €100 = €120/day = €44,000/year revenue at risk.
